steps.title: Prepare lysis buffer and aliquot
steps.instruction: Make lysis buffer containing 100 mmol Tris‑HCl (pH 8.0), 25 mmol EDTA (pH 8.0), 500 mmol NaCl and 1 % SDS, then pipette 1 mL into a tube.

substeps.instruction: Mix the reagents to obtain the buffer composition above.
Aliquot exactly 1 mL of the buffer.

steps.title: Safety precautions and formaldehyde thaw
steps.instruction: Observe safety measures for formaldehyde and thaw it before use.

substeps.instruction: Wear gloves and safety glasses; work inside a fume hood.
Thaw formaldehyde for 1 hour at room temperature.

steps.title: Grind tissue sample
steps.instruction: Process ~200 mg of tissue into a fine powder using liquid nitrogen.

substeps.instruction: Grind the tissue with liquid nitrogen until a powder is obtained.

steps.title: Add sample to lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Transfer the powdered tissue into a 2 mL tube that already contains 1 mL lysis buffer.

steps.title: Incubate lysate
steps.instruction: Digest the sample at 56 °C while mixing periodically.

substeps.instruction: Invert the tube gently every 5–10 minutes.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysate
steps.instruction: After incubation, cool the tube to room temperature and spin down the lysate.

substeps.instruction: Allow the tube to reach room temperature.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Recover DNA by isopropanol precipitation from the aqueous phase.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the aqueous phase to a new 1.5 mL tube.
Add isopropanol equal to 2/3 of the aqueous volume.
Invert the tube at least three times to mix.
Place the tube at –20 °C for 2 hours to precipitate DNA.

steps.title: Pellet wash and supernatant removal
steps.instruction: Collect the DNA pellet by centrifugation and discard the liquid.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA in TE buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve the DNA pellet in TE buffer.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL TE buffer (Roche catalog #5618215001) to the pellet.
Gently mix until the DNA is fully dissolved.
